adaptations_before_results: Size filter: the sketch said 'deal value >= Rs 10 cr OR >= 0.5 % of shares'. A bulk deal is by definition >= 0.5 % of the listed shares, and shares outstanding are not in the data, so the OR clause would admit every bulk deal: the filter is the client's NET value of the session >= Rs 10 crore.
Netting per client and session (BUY - SELL): bulk deals 2021-26 are dominated by HFT / prop desks that buy and sell the same stock the same day; netting removes round trips mechanically.

Intra-group transfers removed (flows_strategies.group_transfer_mask): the data check found ~1,000 2022 block 'institution' buys AND sells that are iShares Mauritius subsidiaries handing shares to iShares ETFs at equal quantity and price (a restructuring, not a flow); found from counts by month / client, no return looked at.

Client classes: fixed keyword list (client_classes), written from the list of the largest client NAMES and counts only. Broker-dealer / ODI / arbitrage names (Societe Generale, BNP Paribas Arbitrage, '- ODI' accounts, Citigroup Global Markets) are not institutions here; family trusts are OTHER (the word TRUST alone is not a keyword).

Index pooling (index_pooling): NIFTY 50 and NIFTY 100 changes pooled into additions / deletions, deduplicated per (stock, effective date); decided before any return because each index alone has far too few events.
Index rows with month-precision effective dates are dropped everywhere; rows without a real announcement date are dropped from the two run-up variants only (counts in data_check).
Effective-date variants enter at the open AFTER the effective date (the sketch allowed 'effective-date close or next open'; the lab fills at next opens).
flowdata.index_changes now also returns announce_source and effective_precision (needed for the availability rule; a file without the columns counts as 'no real announcement').
Stock futures do not fit a Rs 10 lakh account at 1 % risk: the account rows of the short variants will show skipped signals (stated before the run).

availability_rule.deals: a deal dated D is published after D's close: decision at D's close, fill at the next session's open (flowdata.deals with before = D + 1; nsedata.cutoff(D + 1) clips everything)
availability_rule.fo_listed: short variants need a stock future traded on the decision day (F&O bhavcopy, EOD)
availability_rule.index_announcement: only a date exists: assumed published after that date's close; the decision is the first symbol session ON or AFTER the announcement date (announce_date <= decision day), the fill the next session's open (a weekend release fills on the second session after it)
availability_rule.index_effective: effective_date = first session of the new composition; index funds trade at the close of the session before it. Effective-date variants decide at the close of the first symbol session on / after the effective date and fill at the next open
availability_rule.runup_exit: max_hold = sessions from the entry session to the last calendar session before the effective date (exchange calendar, public in advance); exit at that session's close

excluded: PROP_BROKER (prop / HFT / brokers / ODI issuers / arbitrage desks)
OTHER (individuals, companies, promoters, family trusts, banks, unclassified foreign entities)
client_classes.netting: per (session, stock, client name): net = sum(BUY value) - sum(SELL value) over its bulk and block deals that session (value_cr = qty x price / 1e7, unadjusted); a same-day round trip nets to ~0 and does not qualify. Before netting, intra-group transfers are removed: a BUY and a SELL in the same stock and session with equal quantity and price whose client names start with the same word (ignoring THE, M/S) are both dropped
client_classes.rule: client name upper-cased, dots -> spaces, whitespace collapsed; the FIRST class whose regex list matches wins, in this order; no match = OTHER

corporate_action_rule: events_run.drop_excluded: a trade whose (decision day, exit day] holds an unexplained overnight gap or a demerger / scheme / large-rights ex-day is dropped and counted; reported both ways

sources: NSE bulk / block deals historical report (flowdata deals)
NSE Indices month-end constituent files + press releases (flowdata index_changes)
NSE index files (NIFTY Next 50 / 100 / 500 benchmark, report-only)

2023-26.protocol: protocol.evaluate, DISCOVERY 70 % (H1 / H2) + FINAL 30 %, FINAL once and only for screen passers

eras.old_era_look: EVERY variant gets its old-era judgement, whatever its 2023-26 result

expected_from_counts: index events are few: about 6-7 pooled additions and as many deletions per half-yearly review, i.e. well under 60 in the 2023-26 DISCOVERY window; every index variant is therefore expected to FAIL the 2023-26 screen on trade count and cannot be 'proven' (stated before any return was computed). The old era has 58-71 usable pooled events per half (data_check.pooled_index_events), before the member-day, stock-future and one-position-at-a-time rules: at or below the 60-trade minimum, so the trade-count gate may decide the index variants there too

fills_costs.shorts: stock future on the cash price, futures costs, no basis / lot / roll
fills_costs.stops: 20 % catastrophe stop on every variant; exit by the clock

gates.no_relaxation: a variant short of a trade minimum fails on trade count; nothing is pooled, relaxed or re-defined after results

oos.universe: universe_monthly.csv: top 100 by 60-session turnover before each month, gate on decision day

gates.proven: CONFIRMED on 2023-26 FINAL and OOS-CONFIRMED on 2012-23 and DSR >= 0.95 with N = all 2023-26 trials in the ledger (the fair N = this study's 8 variants is also reported)

index_pooling.additions: IN to NIFTY 50 (from anywhere, incl. NIFTY Next 50) or IN to NIFTY 100 (a new NIFTY Next 50 member from outside the top 100); one event per (stock, effective date)
index_pooling.deletions: OUT of NIFTY 50 (incl. demotion to NIFTY Next 50) or OUT of NIFTY 100
index_pooling.month_precision: rows whose effective date is known only to the month are never used (any variant)
index_pooling.not_events: NIFTY Next 50 IN / OUT rows that are only moves to / from NIFTY 50 (already counted as NIFTY 50 deletions / additions)
index_pooling.runup_variants: fl_idx_add_runup and fl_idx_del_rundown use ONLY rows with announce_source == 'press' (a real press-release date); rows dated 'the session before the effective date' are excluded from them (counts in data_check.pooled_index_events)

name: flows_v1
question: Do big-investor bulk / block deals and NIFTY index inclusions / deletions give a tradable edge on NSE stocks after costs, in two eras?

report_only.account: capital.py: Rs 10 lakh, 1 % risk per trade from the stop distance, config.py limits, signals in time order; stock-future lot ~ Rs 7.5 lakh contract
report_only.excess: mean / median excess return per trade vs NIFTY 50 and (mid-cap-fair) NIFTY Next 50, NIFTY 100, NIFTY 500 over each holding window (index open of the entry session -> close of the exit session), 2000 month-block bootstrap resamples
report_only.placebo: deals: every (stock, session) group of deal rows moved to a random session of the same stock in the same era; index changes: every (stock, announcement, effective) group moved to a random session of the same stock and era with the same session gap; same count, same pipeline, seed 20261115
report_only.planted_edge: synthetic mutual-fund net buys of Rs 50 cr dated the session before each stock's best 2 % of 20-session forward returns (old era, member days) must give fl_inst_buy_h20 a large profit and the same rows delayed 25 sessions must not; synthetic NIFTY 50 additions announced on those sessions (effective 21 sessions later) do the same for fl_idx_add_runup

trials: each of the 8 variants is one trial on 2023-26 and one on 2012-23; the 8 report-only twins are recorded as stage 'explore' (they count in N, they cannot be proven)
universe: point-in-time monthly top 500 NSE equity shares by 60-session turnover (events_daily), delisted names kept; a position may be opened only on a member day; index variants trade the changed stocks themselves under the same member-day rule; shorts need a listed stock future

variants.rule: Institution-class client net buyer of >= Rs 10 cr (bulk/block deals of the day): buy next open, 20 sessions
Institution-class client net buyer of >= Rs 10 cr (bulk/block deals of the day): buy next open, 60 sessions
Institution-class client net seller of >= Rs 10 cr: short the stock future next open, 20 sessions
>= 2 distinct institution-class net buyers of >= Rs 10 cr within 10 sessions: buy next open, 20 sessions
NIFTY 50 / NIFTY 100 addition (real announcement date): buy first open after it, sell close before effective
NIFTY 50 / NIFTY 100 addition: short the future at the open after the effective date, 20 sessions
NIFTY 50 / NIFTY 100 deletion: buy at the open after the effective date, 20 sessions
NIFTY 50 / NIFTY 100 deletion (real announcement date): short first open after it, cover close before effective
